analysis: The PR changes only docs/developer/test.md. It bumps the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and, in the head version near lines 173-180, adds a paragraph naming four GLM5Next prompt-policy tests: returnedAssistantReasoningRendersLikeReasoningContent, openRouterReasoningContentReturnRequestsAreServed, capturedOpenRouterToolRequestIsServed and capturedOpenRouterToolServesAFiveStepConversation. These cover OpenRouter returned-reasoning tool turns and replay of captured strict weather-tool requests. No executable code, authorization, attestation, encryption, key handling, cache storage or billing logic changes. The base text I reviewed (units 2-4) matches the patch context. I checked the base doc for security-relevant claims such as SSD cache test isolation, the production-key prohibition, the App Attest tests and the logout tests. None of those sections are modified, so no threat assumption is invalidated. T-041 and the SSD cache mitigations are unaffected. The new test descriptions are consistent with the existing statement that fixtures are synthetic and need no live credentials. Remaining limits: the cited test names and the behaviors they cover (reasoning-content spellings reaching the rendered prompt, coordinator and local HTTP paths) are not in the supplied evidence. Whether those provider-side paths are correct, or whether they alter the prompt-handling attack surface, belongs to the source and test changes in other PR units, if any. This documentation-only change does not itself introduce a regression.
